sources.entry: How to Write Great Outage Post-Mortems

summary.name: How to Write Great Outage Post-Mortems
summary.one_liner: A blog essay from Artsy (Nov 2014) describing how to write a clear, transparent outage post-mortem email, using a multi-hour site outage as the example.
use_cases: Writing an email after a production outage
Structuring an incident timeline and root cause section
Deciding who should write and who should receive outage reports
Keeping a searchable history of past outages
Communicating a crisis to customers and executives without blaming individuals
summary.what_it_does: The page is an essay, not a software tool. It walks through the sections of an outage post-mortem email: a subject line with date and duration, a summary backed by graphs, a timeline of trigger, root cause and consequences, how the outage was resolved, what could have prevented it, and an outage history. It recommends that a senior leader write the report, that recipients be bcc'd, and that outages be filed under a label for later reference. The author illustrates this with a 4-hour outage caused by an AWS-driven server reboot, a MongoDB replica failure, a driver bug, and silenced alerts.
notable: Written by the Artsy engineering team, with a concrete 4-hour outage as the worked example
Advises the most senior engineering leader write the post-mortem to keep focus off individual contributors
Recommends including graphs (the author cites New Relic) so the summary matches the details
caveats: Describes one author's practices and experience; it is not a formal template or standard
